paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the business school of your university is conducting a survey to collect students’ opinions on the express delivery service industry in China. You are to write a response about its recent development and its impact on people’s lives. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您所在大学的商学院正在进行一项调查，收集学生对中国快递服务行业的看法。你要写一篇关于它的最新发展及其对人们生活的影响的回应。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists have known that depriving adult mice of vision can increase the sensitivity of individual neurons (神经元) in the part of the brain devoted to hearing. New research from biologists at the University of Maryland 26 that sight deprivation also changes the way brain cells 27 with one another, shifting the mice’s sensitivity to different frequencies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们已经知道，剥夺成年小鼠的视力可以提高大脑中负责听觉的部分神经元的敏感性。马里兰大学生物学家的新研究表明，视力剥夺也会改变脑细胞相互作用的方式，使小鼠对不同频率的敏感度发生变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: “This study 28 what we are learning about how manipulating vision can have a 29 effect on the ability of an animal to hear long after the window for auditory (听觉的) learning was thought to have 30 ,” said Patrick Kanold, senior author of the study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究的资深作者帕特里克·卡诺德（Patrick Kanold）表示：“这项研究强化了我们正在了解的知识，即在听觉学习窗口被认为已经关闭很久之后，操纵视觉如何对动物的听觉能力产生重大影响。”

paragraphs.sourceText: It was once thought that the sensory regions of the brain were not 31 after a critical period in childhood. This is why children learn languages much more 32 than adults. Kanold’s earlier research disproved this idea by showing that depriving adult mice of vision for a short period increased the sensitivity of individual neurons in the auditory cortex (皮质), which is devoted to hearing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们曾经认为，在童年的关键时期之后，大脑的感觉区域就不再具有适应性。这就是为什么儿童比成人更容易学习语言。卡诺德的早期研究反驳了这一观点，该研究表明，短期剥夺成年小鼠的视力会增加听觉皮层（专门负责听力的）单个神经元的敏感性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Young brains wire themselves according to the sounds they hear frequently, assigning areas of the auditory cortex to 33 frequencies based on what they are used to hearing. The researchers found that, in adult mice, a week in the dark also changed the 34 of space to different frequencies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 年轻的大脑会根据他们经常听到的声音进行自我连接，根据他们习惯听到的声音将听觉皮层区域分配给特定的频率。研究人员发现，在成年小鼠中，在黑暗中呆一周也会将空间分布改变为不同的频率。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We don’t know why we are seeing these patterns,” Kanold said. “We 35 that it may have to do with what the mice are paying attention to while they are in the dark.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们不知道为什么会看到这些模式，”卡诺德说。 “我们推测这可能与老鼠在黑暗中时所注意的事情有关。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Why it’s wrong to look at work-life balance as an achievement
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么将工作与生活的平衡视为一种成就是错误的

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance. The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years — especially for working parents. The concept is often presented as something to achieve, or a goal to reach. And once you’ve reached it, congratulations: you’ve made it; you’re a successful human being of the 21st century.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 很少有话题像工作与生活平衡一样被如此无休止地分析。多年来，对这种神秘状态的追求一直主导着有关职业的讨论——尤其是对于职业父母来说。这个概念通常被表述为要实现的事情或要达到的目标。一旦你达到了目标，恭喜你：你成功了；您是 21 世纪的成功人士。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But the problem is that we often tell ourselves: “I’m going to put in eight hours’ worth of work, and then I’m going to put in eight hours’ worth of ‘me time’, which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything,” says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University. “I don’t think it’s such a simple formula.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但问题是我们经常告诉自己：“我要投入八个小时的工作，然后我要投入八个小时的‘自我时间’，其中包括我的家庭、我的爱好、我的锻炼、我的一切，”纽约大学管理学临床副教授阿纳特·莱赫纳 (Anat Lechner) 说。 “我不认为这是一个如此简单的公式。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) And, according to new findings, it may not be. Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don’t. Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process — a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments. Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is “a cycle, not an achievement”. In their 2020 study, the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms — an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50, all with at least one dependent child — who worked in middle or senior management roles.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 而且，根据新的发现，情况可能并非如此。一些研究人员现在鼓励我们不要再将工作与生活的平衡视为一项要么成功要么失败的成就。相反，他们认为这可能更像是一个终生的过程——一个持续、永无止境的练习，需要自我意识和及时调整。研究人员 Ioana Lupu 和 Mayra Ruiz-Castro 认为，工作与生活的平衡是“一个循环，而不是一项成就”。在 2020 年的研究中，研究人员采访了两家伦敦公司的近 80 名中高级管理职位的员工——年龄在 30 岁至 50 岁之间的男性和女性人数相等，所有人都至少有一名受抚养子女。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here’s what separated them: about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours. The other respondents, meanwhile, all worked long hours because they thought that’s what successful professionals should do.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 虽然听起来受访者有很多共同点，但他们的区别在于：大约 30% 的男性和 50% 的女性表示抵制长时间工作。与此同时，其他受访者都长时间工作，因为他们认为这是成功的专业人士应该做的。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance. They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 卢普和鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗研究了那些拒绝长时间工作的人，他们发现这些工人实际上在保持工作与生活平衡方面有着惊人相似的策略。他们倾向于以自我意识的名义反思和质疑假设，并定期采取措施调整阻碍他们实现工作与生活平衡的事物。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs. First, they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as “I’m a professional, so I should work, work, work”, and asked themselves questions like, “What’s currently causing me stress?” Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions. Did they feel angry, sad, energised? Third, they reprioritised, asking “Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?”, for example. Fourth, they considered their alternatives: is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities? And finally, they implemented changes, like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility, or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) Lupu 和 Ruiz-Castro 确定了研究中工作与生活平衡较好的受访者在工作中使用的五个步骤。首先，他们停下来重新考虑诸如“我是专业人士，所以我应该工作、工作、工作”之类的信念，并问自己诸如“目前是什么给我带来压力？”之类的问题。其次，在确定原因后，他们将注意力集中在由此产生的情绪上。他们是否感到愤怒、悲伤、充满活力？第三，他们重新调整了优先顺序，例如询问“长时间工作真的值得减少家庭时间吗？”。第四，他们考虑了自己的选择：工作中是否有任何可以改变的地方来适应这些新的优先事项？最后，他们实施了一些改变，比如要求主管提供更大的灵活性，或者决定不承担他们遇到的每个项目。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) This five-step process is something anyone can adopt. Going through the steps, and constantly checking in with yourself, can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonise with your personal one. “Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life,” says Lupu.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 任何人都可以采用这个五步流程。完成这些步骤并不断检查自己，可以帮助您转变和调整您的职业生活，使其与您的个人生活更好地协调一致。 “为了确定你想要在工作和生活中做出的改变，了解你的情绪状态至关重要，”卢普说。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) New York University’s Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit. It’s not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work, the gym, kids and chores. If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable. “We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work. We’re not present,” she says. What we call “work-life balance” is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 纽约大学的莱赫纳同意，找到这种平衡是一项持续的追求。这不仅仅是将一天的时间分配给工作、健身房、孩子和家务。如果潜在的压力情绪来源仍然存在，那么您实际上在家度过的时间可能并不愉快。 “我们回到家，尽管我们身体在那里，但精神上我们可能仍在处理工作中发生的事情。我们不在场，”她说。我们所谓的“工作与生活平衡”实际上只是成就感和满足感的替代品。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Of course, finding that balance probably shouldn’t be something you have to do by yourself. Research by Erin Kelly, professor of work and organisation studies at MIT, shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers. For her book Overload: How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do about It, she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）当然，找到这种平衡可能不应该是你必须自己做的事情。麻省理工学院工作与组织研究教授艾琳·凯利的研究表明，公司和管理者可以在为员工创造更好的环境方面发挥关键作用。在她的著作《超载：好工作如何变坏以及如何应对》中，她和合著者 Phyllis Moen 将一家财富 500 强公司的 1,000 多名员工分为两组，一组在管理重新设计下工作，一组继续在现有管理结构内工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Under the management redesign, many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout (精疲力竭). Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees. Workers were allowed to make changes, like cancelling 9 am meetings. All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility, and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to. Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout. They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 在管理重新设计下，采取了许多措施来确保更好的工作与生活平衡并防止精疲力尽。定期提醒经理们明确支持员工。工人们被允许做出改变，比如取消上午 9 点的会议。所有这一切都是为了提高工作满意度和给予员工更大的灵活性，并向员工保证这是管理层的承诺。不出所料，凯利和摩恩发现，重新设计小组的员工压力较小，倦怠程度较低。他们辞职的可能性较小；事实上，在接下来的四年里，他们辞职的可能性比那些继续按照旧政策工作的人低了 40%。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “Work-life balance is understood to be an individual’s response, so people think ‘it’s up to me to manage the craziness of my work life’ ”, says Kelly. But organisations need to examine the demands they’re placing on employees. “The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together. It’s that we have unrealistic expectations of what we’re asked to do on the work side.” If your workplace isn’t an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) “工作与生活的平衡被理解为个人的反应，因此人们认为‘这取决于我来管理我工作生活的疯狂’”，凯利说。但组织需要检查他们对员工提出的要求。 “根本问题不在于工作和生活这两部分如何结合在一起。而是我们对工作方面的要求抱有不切实际的期望。”如果你的工作场所首先就不是一个能够实现工作与生活平衡的环境，那么你在个人层面上为实现这一目标所做的任何努力都将是徒劳的。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) That’s a conversation that appears to be gathering pace. The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives. And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve, the experts say that keeping some perspective can help. For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table. Talking about work-life balance “is a very privileged conversation”, says Lechner. “If we’re reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这场对话似乎正在加快步伐。远程和灵活工作模式的新流行可能会在我们如何平衡职业和个人生活方面发挥重要作用。如果看起来完美的平衡仍然难以实现，专家表示保持一定的视角会有所帮助。对于数百万人来说，工作就是为了养家糊口。莱希纳说，谈论工作与生活的平衡“是一次非常荣幸的对话”。 “如果我们在反思，也许我们也应该反思这一点。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. According to a management expert, work-life balance is not as simple as giving equal amounts of time to work and personal life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 一位管理专家认为，工作与生活的平衡并不只是给予工作和个人生活同等的时间那么简单。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Research found that those who are given greater flexibility at work are less stressed and more likely to stay in their jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 研究发现，那些在工作中获得更大灵活性的人压力更小，更有可能留在工作岗位上。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Workers who rejected working long hours tended to make regular adjustments in order to achieve work-life balance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 拒绝长时间工作的工人往往会定期进行调整，以实现工作与生活的平衡。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Talking about work-life balance is said to be a privilege reserved for the better-off, not for those who barely make a living.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 据说，谈论工作与生活的平衡是富人的特权，而不是那些勉强谋生的人的特权。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Knowing one’s emotional state is of utmost importance in deciding what changes to make for a better work-life balance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 了解自己的情绪状态对于决定做出哪些改变以实现更好的工作与生活平衡至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. More female professionals reported being reluctant to work overtime than their male counterparts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 与男性同行相比，更多女性专业人士表示不愿意加班。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Without organisational support any personal effort to maintain work-life balance will be unsuccessful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 没有组织的支持，任何个人维持工作与生活平衡的努力都不会成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The question of how to achieve work-life balance has long been the main subject of discussion among workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 如何实现工作与生活平衡的问题长期以来一直是工人讨论的主要话题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. You may not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home if you remain occupied with what happened at work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 如果你仍然沉迷于工作中发生的事情，你实际上可能不会在家里体验到情绪健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some researchers suggest that work-life balance is not a goal to achieve, but a process for life to be adjusted promptly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一些研究人员认为，工作与生活的平衡不是一个需要达到的目标，而是一个需要及时调整生活的过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a university student, I’ve come to realise just how little I know about money. I’ve come to the brutal realisation that Australia’s youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一名大学生，我逐渐意识到我对金钱的了解是多么的少。我残酷地认识到，澳大利亚的年轻人由于没有接受任何持续的金融教育而受到了极大的伤害。

paragraphs.sourceText: Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university, I’ve quickly tried to get myself up to speed with the financial terms of the modern era to help manage my personal finances.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一头扎进大学的速成课程后，我很快就试图让自己跟上现代的财务术语，以帮助管理我的个人财务。

paragraphs.sourceText: I’ve read some financial education books, done some online learning, and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我读过一些金融教育书籍，进行了一些在线学习，并与我最亲近的人交谈过他们的金融智慧珍珠。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy, but while I was researching, I still kept wishing that I didn’t have to play catch-up with the money world. I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket!
paragraphs.translationZh: 毫无疑问，对于那些希望提高金融知识的人来说，有数百种优质资源，但在我进行研究时，我仍然希望自己不必追赶金钱世界。我感觉自己在金融的海洋里航行，没有技能，没有救生衣！

paragraphs.sourceText: However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn’t my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，在与有同样想法的朋友交谈后，我很快意识到，并不是我的无知，而是我们的教育系统中缺乏金融教育，导致高中生在现代金钱世界中严重落后。

paragraphs.sourceText: Let’s compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class. On average, English may not be the most popular subject, but it’s consistently on the schedule throughout high school, with all students graduating fluent in English.
paragraphs.translationZh: 让我们将理论金融教育课程与标准必修英语课程进行比较。平均而言，英语可能不是最受欢迎的科目，但它在整个高中的课程表中一直存在，所有学生毕业时都能说流利的英语。

paragraphs.sourceText: A financial education subject should do just the same. It shouldn’t be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a ‘catch up’ phase once we’re out on our own after graduation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 金融教育科目也应该这样做。它不应该只是一个为期一天的活动，而应该是一门贯穿整个高中的课程，让学生逐渐扩大他们的金融知识，并避免毕业后我们独自一人时需要“追赶”阶段。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time, building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge.
paragraphs.translationZh: 就像学习语言或新技能需要时间一样，培养财务技能也需要实践和多年的积累，才能逐渐积累点点滴滴的知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 让年轻人有机会熟悉金钱世界，将为他们提供很大的优势，让他们充满信心和安全地进入成年期，从而能够管理自己的金钱并照顾自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional distress. They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us. We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant!
paragraphs.translationZh: 巧克力可以帮助我们避免很多事情，尤其是情绪困扰。它们在我们遇到麻烦的时候安慰我们，通过向我们体内输送快乐的卡路里来让我们狂跳的心跳平静下来。我们都相信巧克力能让我们立刻感到高兴！

paragraphs.sourceText: Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050! But hey, we have some happy news for you. Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out! If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing, let us tell you the facts. Chocolate trees, whose seeds are used to make chocolate, grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近，科学家声称巧克力可能在 2050 年灭绝，令巧克力爱好者心碎！但是，嘿，我们有一些好消息要告诉你。科学家仍然可以帮助拯救巧克力免于灭绝！如果你不知道为什么科学家会做出关于这个奇妙生物死亡的声明，让我们告诉你事实。巧克力树的种子用于制作巧克力，生长在热带植物世界中，需要非常特定的天气条件才能茂盛。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, fifty percent of the world’s cocoa (可可) beans come from two countries in West Africa: Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8 ℉ temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming, endangering the cacao (可可树) farms in the rainforests. These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife. This will lead to some tough decisions: whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，世界上百分之五十的可可豆来自西非的两个国家：科特迪瓦和加纳。科学家认为，由于全球变暖，到 2050 年，这两个国家的气温将上升 3.8 华氏度，危及雨林​​中的可可树农场。然后，这些农场将不得不转移到凉爽的山区，那里是野生动物的自然栖息地。这将导致一些艰难的决定：是种植巧克力还是拯救野生动物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms’
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，全球变暖危机已经对可可农场产生了严重的负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 产量的增加，导致巧克力的价格飞涨。

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists, however, are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem! They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology, which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，科学家们正在努力寻找一种长期且环保的解决方案来解决这个问题！他们正试图用基因编辑技术改造该物种，将幼苗转变为即使在干燥和温暖的气候下也能生存的物种。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California’s new bio-sciences building, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR. By manipulating the DNA of plants, this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper. Similarly, in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 据《商业内幕》报道，在加州大学新的生物科学大楼里，小型绿色可可树苗排列在冷藏温室中，利用 CRISPR 技术进行新实验。通过操纵植物的 DNA，这项技术已经在世界各地得到应用，使植物变得更坚韧、更便宜。同样，在这项非常规实验中，科学家将对幼苗的 DNA 进行微小而精确的改变，以使可可作物能够在温暖和干燥的气候中生存。
